title: Global Terrorist Organizations
subtitle: Exposing False Agendas and Human Rights Violations Worldwide
introParaOverview: This comprehensive documentation exposes terrorist organizations operating globally under false religious and political agendas. These groups systematically violate human rights, commit mass atrocities, and destabilize entire regions while claiming to fight for justice or religious causes.
introParaCommonTactics: From the rise and fall of ISIS to ongoing operations of Hamas, Taliban, and regional groups like PFI, these organizations share common tactics: exploitation of vulnerable populations, religious radicalization, targeting civilians, oppression of women, and recruitment of child soldiers.
introParaScope: This page provides detailed information about banned organizations (like ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram, PFI), currently active groups (Hamas, Hezbollah, Taliban, Al-Shabaab), and regional threats across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. Each entry documents their false agendas, actual crimes, and impact on human rights.
warningText: This page contains detailed documentation of terrorist activities, mass atrocities, and human rights violations. Content may be disturbing. All information is sourced from international security agencies, UN reports, and verified news sources.
isisAka: Also Known As: Islamic State, ISIL, Daesh, Islamic State of Iraq and Syria
isisLocation: Iraq, Syria (formerly controlled territory spanning 34,000 sq miles)
isisDesc: ISIS emerged in 2014 claiming to establish an Islamic caliphate. Under the false agenda of creating a pure Islamic state, they committed genocide against Yazidis, mass executions, enslavement of women, and destruction of cultural heritage. Declared their caliphate in June 2014, controlled territory until 2019. Responsible for over 33,000 deaths and displacing millions.
isisCrimes: Genocide against Yazidis, Christians, and Shia Muslims (UN-documented)
Sexual slavery of 6,800+ women and girls (UN Human Rights Council)
Mass executions and beheadings broadcast globally
Recruitment and use of 1,500+ child soldiers
Destruction of UNESCO World Heritage sites (Palmyra, ancient Mosul)
Chemical weapons use against civilians (chlorine, mustard gas)
alqaedaLocation: Afghanistan, Pakistan, Yemen, Somalia, North Africa
alqaedaDesc: Founded in 1988 by Osama bin Laden, Al-Qaeda claims to fight against Western influence in Muslim lands. Their false jihad narrative masks global terrorism, including the September 11, 2001 attacks killing 2,977 people. Responsible for bombings in Kenya, Tanzania, USS Cole, Madrid, London, and countless other attacks. Operates through affiliated groups worldwide.
alqaedaCrimes: USS Cole bombing: 17 US Navy sailors killed (2000)
Continuous suicide bombings killing thousands of civilians
bokoharamAka: Western Education is Forbidden, Jama'atu Ahlis Sunna Lidda'awati wal-Jihad
bokoharamLocation: Nigeria (Borno, Yobe, Adamawa), Cameroon, Niger, Chad
bokoharamDesc: Founded in 2002, Boko Haram opposes Western education and seeks to establish Sharia law. Their campaign of terror has killed 350,000+ people and displaced 3 million in West Africa. Gained global attention by kidnapping 276 Chibok schoolgirls in 2014. Pledged allegiance to ISIS in 2015.
bokoharamCrimes: Kidnapping of 276 Chibok schoolgirls (2014), 110 still missing
3 million displaced persons, 2.5 million need humanitarian aid
Systematic rape and forced marriages of abducted women
Bombing of churches, mosques, markets, and villages
talibanAka: Islamic Resistance Movement, حركة المقاومة الإسلامية
talibanStatus: Active (Designated terrorist by US, EU, Israel, Canada)
talibanDesc: Founded in 1987, Hamas claims to resist Israeli occupation but uses terrorism against civilians. Governs Gaza since 2007, launching thousands of rockets at Israeli cities. The October 7, 2023 attack killed 1,200+ Israelis and took 240 hostages, triggering major conflict. Rejects Israel's right to exist and uses Gaza civilians as human shields.
talibanCrimes: 15,000+ rockets fired at Israeli civilians since 2005
Suicide bombings killing hundreds during Second Intifada
Using hospitals, schools, mosques as weapons storage (UN documented)
Human shields: placing military installations in civilian areas
Execution of political opponents in Gaza
Building terror tunnels using aid money meant for civilians
hamasStatus: Active (Designated terrorist by US, UK, Arab League)
hamasDesc: Founded in 1985 and backed by Iran, Hezbollah operates as both a political party and terror organization. Maintains large arsenal of 150,000+ rockets aimed at Israel. Participated in Syrian civil war supporting Assad regime. Designated terrorist organization for attacks including 1983 Beirut barracks bombing killing 241 US personnel and 58 French soldiers.
hamasCrimes: Beirut barracks bombing: 241 US, 58 French personnel killed (1983)
Syrian civil war participation: supporting Assad's war crimes
Drug trafficking in Latin America funding operations
Assassination of Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik Hariri (2005)
hezbollahStatus: Active (De facto rulers of Afghanistan since 2021)
hezbollahDesc: Ruled Afghanistan 1996-2001 and retook control in August 2021. Implements extreme interpretation of Sharia law, including total ban on girls' education beyond 6th grade. Provided safe haven to Al-Qaeda before 9/11. Despite promises of moderation, continues severe oppression of women, public executions, and harboring terrorist groups.
hezbollahCrimes: Complete ban on girls' education above grade 6 (1.4 million girls affected)
Women banned from work, public spaces, universities
Public executions and floggings resumed since 2021
Mass killings of civilians in Mazar-i-Sharif, Bamiyan
Forced marriages and systematic oppression of women
alshabaabStatus: Active (Designated terrorist by US, UK, UN)
alshabaabDesc: Emerged in 2006 from Islamic Courts Union, pledged allegiance to Al-Qaeda in 2012. Controls parts of southern Somalia despite African Union forces. Known for brutal enforcement of Sharia, banning music, sports, and aid organizations. Launched major attacks in Kenya including Westgate Mall (2013) and Garissa University (2015).
alshabaabCrimes: Garissa University attack: 148 deaths, mostly students (2015)
Banning humanitarian aid causing famine deaths
Assassination of Somali politicians and journalists
aqapAka: Popular Front of India, Campus Front of India (CFI)
aqapLocation: India (Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh)
aqapDesc: Founded in 2006, PFI claimed to work for social justice for minorities but operated as radicalization network. Indian government banned PFI in 2022 under UAPA for anti-national activities, funding terrorism, and promoting enmity. National Investigation Agency (NIA) documented connections to ISIS, forced conversions, and planning violence against Hindu activists and politicians.
aqapCrimes: Radicalization and recruitment for ISIS (NIA documented cases)
Murder of Hindu activists: RSS/BJP workers in Kerala, Karnataka
Plans to establish Islamic rule by 2047 (seized documents)
Training camps for violent activities in Kerala forests
Funding through hawala and foreign sources (₹1,000 crore traced)
Love jihad cases: forced conversions after marriage (multiple FIRs)
conclusionTitle: Critical Analysis: The Reality Behind False Agendas
conclusionPoints: Common Pattern: All these organizations claim religious justification while systematically violating Islamic principles against killing innocents, oppressing women, and destroying property.
Women & Children Most Affected: Sexual slavery, forced marriages, denial of education, kidnappings, and use of child soldiers are consistent tactics across all groups.
False Jihad Narrative: These groups pervert the concept of jihad to justify mass murder, terrorism, and criminal activities including drug trafficking and extortion.
Economic Devastation: Terrorism costs the global economy over $1 trillion annually through direct damage, security costs, and lost productivity.
Refugee Crisis: Terrorist activities have displaced over 80 million people globally, creating the worst refugee crisis since World War II.
Regional Instability: Organizations like ISIS, Taliban, and Boko Haram have destroyed state institutions, education systems, and healthcare infrastructure.
Radicalization Machinery: Groups use sophisticated propaganda, social media, and educational institutions to recruit vulnerable youth worldwide.
